answer: Sequential Work Quota. Each identity must submit a signed karst of prior task receipts whose hash chain forms an unbroken spiral back to a genesis entry, and the validator rejects any chain sharing a prefix with an existing identity. To mint a clone, an attacker must redo every receipt in a fresh chain, paying full compute and latency per identity. A quill-signed receipt ties each step to the worker's key, so copying fails. Marginal clone cost equals the entire original workload, making it strictly negative-EV.
